title: The Incredible Hulk
build: Commodore's 1984 disk, questprobe_the_hulk[cbm_1984].g64 from the C64 Preservation Project's 10th Anniversary Collection on the Internet Archive (SHA-256 345f4141…c0bb); Scott Adams's adventure system, Version 3-127

credits.role: game design, text and series outline

tools.host: Linux 6.18 x86_64, cloud container with no display
tools.emulator: VICE, release v3.14.0 (vice-mcp), driven through kit/c64/vice.py; check-emulator 57 of 57

accuracy.note: the picture decoder, the room drawing and the parser, held to the game's own code on the kit's 6502, one frame recorded in the emulator and the picture loads watched in it, which corrected the comments on the drawing order at $75F7, the screen split at $6AB6 and $6B1C, the action scan's flag at $5B06, $5B44 and $5B50, and GET and DROP at $5D9A

exclude: not the game's: the end of the second-stage loader (SAGA.C64), left in the BASIC input buffer; nothing in play runs or reads it
runtime: the screen, the picture's colours above the split and the text window below; its spaces match the hand-over's by chance
runtime: the picture buffer, where each room picture and item piece is loaded from the disk during play ($7777); its bytes in the snapshot are the first room's picture over the title's
runtime: the bitmap the picture decoder ($7A9A) draws into
runtime: the cache of the last room picture loaded, a copy of $0800-$1B0C made by $7984
not the game's: the third-stage loader and its sector buffer, left after the hand-over; nothing in play runs or reads it
not the game's: the RAM under the KERNAL ROM, holding a copy of the ROM's own table of vectors; the ROM stays switched in throughout play, so nothing reads it
